# Handoff — Site Selection & Webots Replay for the Hybrid Indoor-Localization Dataset

**Project:** Real WiFi + IMU (from Microsoft / XYZ10 Indoor Location Competition 2.0) fused with synthetic wheel-odometry + camera generated by replaying real trajectories on a TIAGO++ in Webots R2025a.
**Source dataset (locked):** Indoor Location Competition 2.0.
**Status:** Dataset chosen. This doc tells you how to (a) pick the 3 working sites and (b) reconstruct + replay them in Webots.

---

## 0. Read this first — why there are no hard-coded "3 site IDs" in this doc

The full dataset is **204 buildings released as anonymized hash IDs** (e.g. `5dd3d7732a57a34356595932`). Microsoft/XYZ10 publish **no catalog of geometry** — there is no public list saying "site X has loops, site Y has hard turns." Therefore the only correct way to choose 3 sites with rich, varied paths (straight runs, smooth turns, hard turns, loops) is to **measure the trajectories after download**. A runnable scorer (`select_sites.py`, shipped with this doc) does exactly that and produces an auditable ranking. Do not skip it — the picks must come from the data, not from a name.

Your job: download → run the scorer → confirm the suggested 3 → reconstruct them in Webots.

---

## 1. Verified facts (checked against the official repo, do not re-derive)

- **Download (full 60 GB):** `https://aka.ms/location20dataset` (Microsoft Research). Sample + parser code: `https://github.com/location-competition/indoor-location-competition-20` (Kaggle mirror: `https://www.kaggle.com/c/indoor-location-navigation`).
- **License:** MIT (repo `LICENSE`). Redistribution + modification permitted — fine for a derived hybrid dataset, keep the attribution.
- **Trace file** = one `*.txt` per surveyor walk, tab-separated, one row per sensor event. Column 1 = Unix time (ms); column 2 = type. The ten types and the rows we use:
  - `TYPE_WAYPOINT  x  y` — **ground-truth (x, y) in METRES**, surveyor-labeled at landmarks. This is our GT polyline and the replay target.
  - `TYPE_WIFI  ssid  bssid  rssi  frequency  lastSeenTimestamp` — **one row per AP**; a "scan" = all `TYPE_WIFI` rows sharing one column-1 timestamp (full multi-AP fingerprint, not strongest-AP).
  - `TYPE_ACCELEROMETER / TYPE_GYROSCOPE / TYPE_MAGNETIC_FIELD / TYPE_ROTATION_VECTOR` — cols 3–5 = x,y,z, col 6 = accuracy. IMU runs at **~50 Hz** (confirmed in the MobiCom'23 paper). Uncalibrated variants carry 6 values + accuracy.
  - `TYPE_BEACON` — iBeacon; ignore for this project.
- **Per floor** you also get: `floor_image.png` (raster plan), `floor_info.json` (`map_info.width`/`height` in **metres**), `geojson_map.json` (**vector floor plan** — this is what you extrude into Webots walls).
- **Coordinate frame:** waypoints, `floor_info` dimensions, and the GeoJSON are all in the **same metric frame**, origin at the floor-plan corner. No cross-modal alignment needed — they already share one frame.
- **Known-good smoke-test site (verified to exist in the repo):** `5dd3d7732a57a34356595932` — name *杭州西溪银泰城* (Hangzhou Xixi Yintai City), floors `B1` and `F1`. Use it to validate the whole pipeline before committing to the final 3. **Caveat:** it is a shopping mall (curved storefronts) — good for a smoke test, not necessarily a final pick.

---

## 2. Selection criteria → measurable thresholds

The scorer turns "enough data, not too long, not too small, smooth rich paths" into numbers. Defaults (all editable at the top of `select_sites.py`):

| Goal | Metric | Default band |
|---|---|---|
| Enough data | traces per floor | ≥ 15 (so you can hold out ~20%) |
| Not too small | floor area (`width × height`) | 200–3000 m² |
| Not too long / not too tiny | **median** trace length | 30–150 m |
| Straight lines present | share of near-straight vertices (<20°) | 30–85% (some, not all) |
| Smooth turns present | share 20–70° | ≥ ~12% |
| Hard turns present | share >70° | ≥ ~8% |
| Loops present | traces with a grid-revisit | ≥ ~15% of traces |
| WiFi usable | median APs/scan; median scan interval | ≥ 20 APs; ≤ 6 s |
| Webots-buildable | `geojson_map.json` present | required (hard filter) |

Geometry is measured on the **waypoint polyline** (metric GT). Waypoints cluster at corners, so they're well-suited to turn detection but sparse — fine for ranking. If you later want finer turn stats, recompute on the step-detected path from the repo's `compute_f.py`; don't change the ranking logic for it.

---

## 3. How to select (run this)

```bash
# 1. Download + unzip the full dataset so you have  <root>/data/<siteID>/<floor>/...
# 2. Score every floor:
python select_sites.py /path/to/iln20/data --csv site_features.csv --top 20
```

Output: a ranked table on stdout, a full `site_features.csv` (every floor, every sub-score — auditable), and a **suggested diverse top-3** that deliberately spans one straight-dominant, one loop-rich, and one hard-turn-rich floor so the synthetic set covers every path type you asked for.

**Locking the 3:**
1. Start from the suggested diverse top-3.
2. Hard-reject any floor with `has_geojson = False` (can't build walls) or `med_imu_hz < 40` (should be ~50).
3. Sanity-check `med_aps_per_scan ≥ 20` and `med_wifi_interval_s` is small. **Expect WiFi to be the weak axis** (see §6) — prefer the densest-WiFi floors among otherwise-good candidates.
4. Open each candidate's `floor_image.png` and confirm the walls are mostly **rectilinear** (straight corridors, box rooms). Down-rank curved atria / glass / heavy clutter — those are slow to model and off-spec.
5. Aim for **variety across the 3**: e.g. one long straight-corridor floor, one with a clean loop, one with several hard 90° turns.

---

## 4. Webots reconstruction (per chosen floor)

1. **World frame:** set `WorldInfo.coordinateSystem "ENU"` (z-up). Then dataset `x → Webots x`, dataset `y → Webots y`, height `→ z`. This makes waypoints drop in with zero rotation.
2. **Walls from GeoJSON:** parse `geojson_map.json`; each wall polygon/segment becomes a `Solid` with a `Box`/extruded geometry, height ~2.7 m, thickness ~0.1–0.2 m. Place at the polygon's metric coordinates directly. Keep it to straight walls + simple boxes — do not model furniture.
3. **Floor:** a single textured `Floor`/plane sized to `floor_info.json` width × height, optionally texture-mapped with `floor_image.png` for visual realism (scale = image px ÷ metric width).
4. **Scale check:** drop two waypoints from a trace as markers and confirm they land on the right spots over the floor texture before proceeding. A 1–2 m offset means the GeoJSON/image origin convention is flipped — fix the origin, not the data.

---

## 5. Trajectory replay + synthetic stream generation

**Master clock = the real trace timestamps.** Everything synthetic is generated on that timeline so the hybrid sample stays time-aligned across all four modalities.

1. **Path:** take the trace's `TYPE_WAYPOINT` sequence (t, x, y). Interpolate a smooth, C¹-continuous path through them (Catmull–Rom or cubic spline) parameterized by the real timestamps. This gives a continuous pose target between sparse landmarks.
2. **Drive the TIAGO++:** recommended approach for a clean replay — use a **Supervisor** to set the mobile base pose along the interpolated path (guarantees the synthetic camera/odometry correspond exactly to the real GT), while computing differential-drive wheel velocities by inverse kinematics so the **wheel encoders produce realistic odometry** (with the small slip/quantization Webots introduces). Alternative: closed-loop velocity control toward the path — more realistic odometry drift, but adds tracking error vs GT; only use if reviewers specifically want emergent drift.
3. **Synthetic wheel odometry:** read wheel encoder positions each step; integrate to (x, y, θ). Log at ~50–100 Hz.
4. **Synthetic camera:** mount the TIAGO++ head camera; capture RGB (and depth, since TIAGO has an RGB-D head) at a fixed rate (10 or 30 fps). Log frame + timestamp.
5. **Carry the real streams through unchanged:** real WiFi scans, real IMU, real waypoints keep their original timestamps. Resample all modalities to whatever common grid your model wants, but keep the raw timestamps too.

---

## 6. Watch-outs (will bite you if ignored)

- **WiFi cadence is the weak point.** Android throttles background WiFi scans (≈4 scans / 2 min on Android ≥8), so per-site WiFi can be well below 1 Hz — sparser than IMU by orders of magnitude. The scorer reports `med_wifi_interval_s`; pick the densest available and plan to **forward-fill / interpolate WiFi** onto the common timeline. Don't expect 0.5 Hz everywhere.
- **Malls dominate the dataset** (curved fronts, atria, glass). The rectilinear-floor check in §3 step 4 is not optional — it's the main filter between "easy Webots build" and "two days of tracing."
- **Kaggle private-test labels were never released.** Use the **labeled training corpus** (waypoints present) for everything; ignore the unlabeled competition test split.
- **Waypoints are sparse and at landmarks**, not a dense GT track. That's fine (you interpolate), but don't treat raw waypoint spacing as the sampling rate of your GT.
- **Frame origin convention** (image top-left vs metric bottom-left, y-flip) is the single most common reconstruction bug — the 2-marker scale check in §4 step 4 catches it.

---

## 7. Acceptance checklist (definition of done for the 3 sites)

- [ ] 3 floors locked, each: ≥15 traces, area 200–3000 m², median trace 30–150 m, `geojson_map.json` present, IMU ~50 Hz.
- [ ] The 3 span the geometry types (straight-dominant / loop / hard-turn) per the scorer.
- [ ] `site_features.csv` archived alongside the chosen IDs (the audit trail for why these 3).
- [ ] Each floor reconstructed in Webots (ENU, walls from GeoJSON, scaled floor) with the 2-marker scale check passing.
- [ ] One full trace per floor replayed: synthetic odometry + RGB(-D) logged on the real timestamps, real WiFi/IMU/waypoints passed through, all resampleable to one timeline.
- [ ] WiFi interval per site recorded; interpolation strategy noted.

## 8. Deliverables back to the project

1. The 3 chosen `siteID/floor` pairs + `site_features.csv`.
2. Webots world file(s) per floor (`.wbt`) + the GeoJSON→walls importer script.
3. The replay script (spline + Supervisor drive) and the per-trace synthetic logs (odometry, RGB-D) with timestamps.
4. A one-page note: per-site WiFi cadence, any geometry simplifications made, and the frame-alignment offset used.
